questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n!}{3^n}$$

II. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^2 + 1}$$

III. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n + 1}$$

options.why: Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Correct. I: diverges (ratio test gives L = ∞). II: diverges (limit comparison with the harmonic series). III: diverges (terms approach 1, not 0 (nth term test)).
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.

questions.explanation: Series I diverges: ratio test gives L = ∞. Series II diverges: limit comparison with the harmonic series. Series III diverges: terms approach 1, not 0 (nth term test).

This forgets the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$ from $$du = 2x\,dx$$.
After substituting, the limits must change to u-values (from c to 1 + c), not stay 0 to 1.
